# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 19 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 19 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_019_page_001.jpg

---

**19:1** But wrath without mercy came upon the ungodly to the very end; for God foreknew even their future —

**19:2** that, having themselves permitted the departure of the Israelites and having sent them forth with great urgency, they would repent and pursue them.

**19:3** For while they were still engaged in mourning, and lamenting at the graves of the dead, they took up another senseless plan; and they pursued as fugitives those whom they had expelled with entreaties.

**19:4** For the fate that they deserved was drawing them to this end, and made them forget what had happened, so that they might complete the punishment which was still lacking to their torments.

**19:5** And that your people might pass through the water by a miraculous way, while they themselves found a strange death.

**19:6** For the whole creation in its natural order was fashioned anew, serving your specific commands, so that your children might be kept unharmed.

**19:7** The cloud was seen shadowing the camp, and dry land arising where water had been before; an open road out of the Red Sea and a grassy plain out of the violent surge;

**19:8** through which the whole nation passed that was protected by your hand, having seen miraculous wonders.

**19:9** For they grazed like horses, and they leaped about like lambs, praising you, O Lord, who had delivered them.

**19:10** For they still remembered the things of their sojourn: how instead of cattle the land brought forth gnats, and instead of fish the river swarmed with countless frogs.

**19:11** But afterward they also saw a new birth of birds, when carried by craving they demanded delicacies of food;

**19:12** for, as a consolation, quails came up from the sea for them.

**19:13** And the punishments came upon the sinners not without prior signs given in the violence of thunder; for they suffered justly according to their own wickedness, since they practiced a bitterer hatred toward strangers.

**19:14** For some did not receive strangers who were unknown to them, but others had enslaved guests who were their benefactors.

**19:15** And not only this; but there will be some other judgment for the others, since they received them with hostility; for the Sodomites treated as enemies those who came to them as strangers.

**19:16** But these — after they had welcomed the Israelites with festivity, and had made them partners by the same rights — later afflicted them with hard labors.

**19:17** And they were struck with blindness, as also those at the door of the righteous man, when, covered with impenetrable darkness, each man sought the passage through his own door.

**19:18** For the elements rearranged themselves with one another, just as the notes on a harp vary the character of the melody while the rhythm remains the same; and that is what can be carefully inferred from the sight of what happened.

**19:19** For land creatures became water creatures, and swimming creatures moved over to dry land.

**19:20** Fire maintained its own power in the water, and water forgot its own quenching nature.

**19:21** On the other hand, flames did not parch the flesh of perishable creatures going about among them, nor did they melt the easily-melted crystalline kind of heavenly food.

**19:22** For in everything, O Lord, you magnified and glorified your people, and did not neglect to help them in every time and place.
